Facts, in short, necessary for disposal of the appeal may be stated thus : two suits being Title Suit No. 55 of 1961/ 80 of 1962 and Partition Suit No. 25 of 1961/79 of 1962 between the same parties were heard analogously and disposed of by one judgment and separate decrees. The appellants instituted Title Suit No. 55 of 1961 on February 17, 1961 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Third Court, Comilla which on transfer to the court of Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla was renumbered as Title Suit No. 80 of 1962, for confirmation of their possession and for a declaration of their title that the property described in schedule (1) to the plaint were the self-acquired property of Kala Gazi and not of the father of Kala Gazi as claimed by the plaintiffs of the portion suit. Respondents 1 to 23 instituted Partition Suit No. 25 of 1961 on February 29, 1961 in the 3rd Court of the Subordinate Judge which on transfer to the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla was renumbered as Partition Suit No. 79 of 1962. The case of the said plaintiffs, inter alia, is that all the lands described in the schedules 1 to 4 to the plaint belonged to two brothers, Ashok Gazi and Kala Gazi in equal shares. Ashok Gazi died leaving behind two sons Jinnat Ali and Ashraf Ali who inherited 4 annas share each in the case land. Thereafter Jinnat Ali died leaving behind the plaintiffs 1 to 17 and Ashraf Ali died leaving behind the plaintiffs 18 to 23. Thus the plaintiffs 1 to 23 collectively inherited 8 annas share in the entire case land. On the other hand Kala Gazi died leaving behind two sons Fazle Ali, predecessor of defendants 1 to 3, and Tamizuddin predecessor of defendants 4 to 8. Thus the defendants 1 to 8 collectively inherited 8 annas share in the entire suit property. The partition suit was contested by the defendants 1, 4, 5 and 6 by filing a joint written statement. There was no dispute with regard to the lands described in schedules 2, 3 and 4. The dispute was in respect of the property described in schedule 1 only. The defendants claimed that the property described in schedule were the self-acquired property of their predecessor Kala Gazi who acquired the same by a patta dated 4th Flagon, 1293 B.S. Both the suits were disposed of by one judgment dismissing the title suit and decreeing the partition suit on the finding that the schedule property in the partition suit was not the self-acquired property of Kala Gazi but belonged to the father of Kala Gazi. The appellants who were the defendants in the partition suit filed an appeal against the decree passed in the partition suit but they did not file any appeal against the decree dismissing their title suit. At the hearing of the appeal the learned Judges of the High Court accepted the contention of the respondents that the question regarding the appellants claim to schedule 1 property on the ground that the properties were the self-acquired property of Kala Gazi, could not be agitated in the appeal, because, the appellants were estopped from raising this question, inasmuch as, the issue was decided in the title suit itself, wherein it was held by the trial court that the properties of schedule 1 to the plaint in the title suit were not the self-acquired property of Kala Gazi but were the properties belonged to the common ancestor of the parties, namely, father of Kala Gazi. On this finding the appeal was dismissed. 

 9. Contest in both the suits was with regard to the first schedule lands and there was no controversy with regard to the lands of other 3 schedules. Defendants in the partition suit who were the plaintiffs in the title suit claimed the entire first schedule property with the exception of plots 578 and 579 measuring 93 decimals as belonging exclusively to them. With regard to the first schedule property their case is that the lands comprising of five plots measuring 4.97 acres was acquired by a patta dated 4th Falgoon, 1293 B.S. by Kala Gazi alone and it was his exclusive property; and that Kala Gazi out of sympathy allowed his brother Ashok Gazi to possess 93 decimals of plots 578 and 579. The plaintiffs in the partition suit who were the defendants in the title suit claimed that all the lands of "Ka", "Kha" and "Ga" schedules of the title suit were the ejmali properties of their predecessors Jinnat Ali, Ashraf Ali, Fazle Ali and Tamizuddin in equal shares.
